Avodah Zarah 66b:3:1.english: Bat Tiha: A hole that they make in the stopper of a barrel to smell the wine, to check if it can last. For a gentile to smell a Jew's wine, it is permitted.

Avodah Zarah 66b:7.english: The Gemara answers: Abaye could say to you that Rabbi Yehuda also holds that a smell is a substantial matter. Wasn’t it stated with regard to that mishna that Rabba bar bar Ḥana says that Reish Lakish says: In the case of a hot loaf of bread and an open barrel, everyone agrees that it is forbidden, as the bread certainly absorbed of the smell of the wine?

Avodah Zarah 67a:1.english: Furthermore, in the case of a cool loaf of bread and a stoppered barrel, everyone agrees that it is permitted. They disagree only with regard to the case of a hot loaf of bread and a stoppered barrel, or in the case of a cool loaf of bread and an open barrel. And this case of mine, i.e., the case of the bunghole, is also comparable to the case of a hot loaf of bread and an open barrel, in which everyone agrees that the bread is forbidden.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 66a:11:1.hebrew: חלא שנפל לגו חמרא: חלא דאיסור לגו חמרא דהיתר, דברי הכל בנותן טעם. דכי נפיל לגויה, לא הוי דמי ליה לא בריחא ולא בטעמא, שאין היין מבטל ריח החומץ עד שנתרבה לתוכו, ולא החומץ מבטל ריח היין משום דרובא חמרא.
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 66a:11:1.english: **Forbidden vinegar that fell into wine**: Forbidden vinegar into permitted wine, all agree that it is forbidden if it imparts flavor. For when it falls into it, it is not similar to it neither in smell nor in taste, as the wine does not nullify the smell of the vinegar until it is greatly increased within it, and the vinegar does not nullify the smell of the wine because most of it is wine.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 66a:11:2.hebrew: אבל חמרא לגו חלא: משעה שהגיע לאויר הכלי, נהפך היין בריחו לריח החומץ, וקודם שנתערבו היו שוין בריחן.
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 66a:11:2.english: **But wine into vinegar**: From the moment it reached the airspace of the vessel, the wine's smell turned into the smell of vinegar, and before they mixed, they were equal in their smell.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 66b:1:1.hebrew: ריחיה חלא: יין זה סמוך לעירובו היה ריחיה חלא וטעמיה חמרא, ובתר ריחיה אזלינן. וכשנתערבו, הוה ליה מין במינו.
Rashi on Avodah Zarah 66b:1:1.english: **Whose smell is vinegar**: This wine, near its mixing, had a smell of vinegar and a taste of wine, and we follow its smell. And when they mixed, it became a type with its own type.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 66b:4:1.english: The bread is permitted: To non-priests.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 66b:4:2.english: That it does not have the taste of cumin but only the smell of cumin: And if it is because it was heated, it does not matter, for teruma's prohibition is not a prohibition of benefit.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 66b:5:1.english: Rabbi Meir deems it forbidden: Because it absorbed the smell of the wine.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 66b:6:1.english: According to Rava: Who says that a smell is nothing, it is certainly by force that he said his statement as a tannaic dispute, and it is not a universally accepted matter, for Rabbi Meir deems it forbidden, and there is no other reason to say it is forbidden except because of the smell.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 66b:6:2.english: According to Abaye: Who says that a smell is a substantial matter.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 66b:6:3.english: Shall we say it is a tannaic dispute?: Do we say that Rabbi Yehuda does not agree with Abaye? Or perhaps he always agrees with him, and Rabbi Yehuda's reason here is that he holds that the smell of wine does not enter the bread, but regarding the bat tiha, where the smell of nesekh wine enters the body, he agrees (that it is forbidden).

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 67a:1:1.english: Everyone agrees it is forbidden: For the smell certainly entered it.

Rashi on Avodah Zarah 67a:1:2.english: And this case of mine: This bat tiha that I prohibited is comparable to a hot loaf of bread and an open barrel.

Shulchan Arukh, Yoreh De'ah 134:6.english: If vinegar belonging to a gentile fell into permitted wine, or wine belonging to a gentile fell into permitted vinegar, it is forbidden if it imparts flavor.

Steinsaltz on Avodah Zarah 66a:11.english: Abaye and Rava further disagreed on this matter. First, they preface: If **vinegar into wine** [forbidden vinegar fell into a barrel of wine], **everyone agrees** that it is forbidden **if it imparts flavor**. But if **wine into vinegar** [wine fell into a barrel of vinegar], since due to the abundance and sharpness of the vinegar it affects the wine, such that its smell becomes like the smell of vinegar even before it mixed with the vinegar, **Abaye says**: it is forbidden **by any amount**, and **Rava says**: it is forbidden **if it imparts flavor**.

Tosafot on Avodah Zarah 66a:11:1.hebrew: ורבא אמר בנותן טעם ריחיה חלא וטעמא חמרא חמרא: תימה, דקיימא לן כרבא לגבי אביי, וקיימא לן כרבי יהושע בן לוי נמי, דאמר בפרק המוכר פירות (בבא בתרא דף צו.) דריחיה חלא וטעמא חמרא חלא. ורבי יוחנן אמר דריחיה חלא וטעמא חמרא חמרא (כרב כהנא). ויש לומר דהתם איכא לישנא אחרינא, ודרומאי מתני איפכא, דרבי יוחנן אמר ריחיה חלא וטעמיה חמרא חלא, ורבי יהושע בן לוי אמר חמרא כרבא דהכא. ומכאן נראה דמותר לקדש בערב שבת על היין שריחו חלא וטעמיה חמרא.
Tosafot on Avodah Zarah 66a:11:1.english: **And Rava says it is forbidden if it imparts flavor, for a liquid whose smell is vinegar and its flavor is wine is considered wine**: It is puzzling, for this ruling contradicts another ruling, as we hold in accordance with Rava against Abaye, and we also hold in accordance with Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi, who said in the chapter 'He Who Sells Produce' (Bava Batra page 96) that a liquid whose smell is vinegar and its flavor is wine is considered vinegar. And Rabbi Yochanan said that a liquid whose smell is vinegar and its flavor is wine is considered wine (like Rav Kahana). And it can be said that there is another version there, and the southerners teach the opposite: that Rabbi Yochanan said a liquid whose smell is vinegar and its flavor is wine is considered vinegar, and Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said it is wine, like Rava here. And from here it seems that it is permitted to recite Kiddush on Friday evening over wine whose smell is vinegar and its flavor is wine.
